published 2023 | The DGVs are expressed in terms of the active ingredient (alpha-cypermethrin) and do not relate to any of the breakdown products of alpha-cypermethrin. The DGVs are below current analytical limits of reporting for alpha-cypermethrin. However, the available toxicity data indicate that toxic effects can occur below the current limits of reporting. See Accounting for local conditions for guidance on what to do if DGVs are below analytical detection limits. Given that routine pesticide analyses cannot discriminate between the two isomers that make up alpha-cypermethrin from the other six isomers of cypermethrin, it is recommended that the cypermethrin concentration of the sample, which represents the sum of all isomers, is compared with the alpha-cypermethrin DGVs. If the cypermethrin concentration exceeds the relevant DGV, further investigation is required, which could include a more complex analysis specific to alpha-cypermethrin.

published 2023 | Low reliability guideline values are typically not adequate to assess water quality, but can be used as interim values until more reliable values are derived. If used as interim values, they should always be used in conjunction with other lines of evidence. See Application of default guideline values for more information. Some of the DGVs may be below current analytical limits of reporting for BPA. However, the available toxicity data indicate that toxic effects can occur below the current limits of reporting. See Accounting for local conditions for guidance on what to do if DGVs are below analytical detection limits. Comparison of the DGVs with the available toxicity data indicated that the 95%, 90% and 80% species protection DGVs may not adequately protect some species. If there are concerns that the DGV for a specific ecosystem condition and associated level of protection may not offer sufficient protection for key species in the water body of interest, a conservative application of the DGVs may be warranted. For example, the 99% species protection DGV for BPA could be applied to a slightly-to-moderately disturbed ecosystem.
